neighbours.label: National modifier (adjective or country possessive) naming a government agency or public funding body (the German Research Foundation, Japan's Ministry), vs the same nationality words before ordinary nouns
fire: The survey was carried out with a grant from the Norwegian Research Council.
Funding for the telescope came partly from the Italian Space Agency.
Our partners include France's Ministry of Agriculture and two universities.
The vaccine trial was paid for by the Dutch Organisation for Scientific Research.
Last spring the team received support from the Australian Research Council.
The rescue effort was coordinated with India's Department of Space.
This work was sponsored by the Danish National Research Foundation.
Additional money was provided by the Korean Ministry of Science and ICT.
quiet: At the market we bought Norwegian salmon and a loaf of rye bread.
The film follows an Italian chef who opens a small restaurant in Boston.
Every summer, France's beaches fill with tourists from across Europe.
The garden was planted with Dutch tulips in long, bright rows.
Last spring the team signed an Australian goalkeeper on a two-year deal.
The novel describes India's monsoon season through the eyes of a farmer.
She knitted a sweater in a traditional Danish pattern for her nephew.
Our neighbours cooked Korean barbecue in the backyard on Saturday.

predictions: Funding or agency sentences reach 0.5-1.1 at the nationality token; nationality words before food, people or places stay under 0.3.
notes: Card: ' German' x5, ' Australian' x4, possessive 's x6 before Research Foundation, Space Agency, Department for International Development. Probe: Japan's Ministry 1.137, German Research Foundation 0.813, Swiss National Science Foundation 0.650, Canadian Space Agency 0.554; German sausages 0.023, Swedish striker 0.063, Australian coastline 0.288, local foundation 0.220.
